correctness.rationale: For a,b>=2 the two terminal cliques are exactly the maximal cliques of order at least three. The sole connector is their intersection at ell=1. Otherwise the unique connecting path identifies the two connector vertices and path positions; any orbit merger must preserve these data up to interchange of equal sides. Independent leaf permutations and, for equal sides, reflection realize all stated orbits. Stable colors are automorphism-invariant and distinguish distances to any stable cell or stable union by iterative neighborhood counts. At ell=1 degrees suffice. For unequal a>b and ell>=2 the degree-(a+1) singleton separates spine positions by distance; the only possible left-leaf collision is with p_1, resolved by degrees except at ell=2 and a=b+1, when the neighboring degree multiplicities differ. When a=b>=3, degrees distinguish leaves, connectors and interiors, and distances to the connector pair separate interior reflection orbits. When a=b=2, ell=2 has no interiors and ell=3 has one with two connector neighbors. At ell>=5 the first interior pair has a distance-two neighbor, unlike the leaves, and the rest are separated by distance. At ell=4 the degree-(3,2) cells are equitable with neighbor counts (0,3) and (1,1) respectively, whereas the four leaves and two interior vertices are distinguished by triangle membership. This proves the exception [2,6] versus [2,2,4] and exhausts the domains. Independent finite replay: python3 /workspace/check_frozen_mathematics.py 1, testing the 27 cases with 2<=a<=b<=3 and 1<=ell<=9 by ordered partition splitting and exhaustive testing of color-preserving permutations for automorphisms. It finds exactly the stated exception and verifies its sizes without relying on an orbit formula for those automorphisms. The recorded source checks cover 2730 triples by the orbit formula and a second method on 63 of those triples; these and the independent sample are finite corroboration only.

value.rationale: The family isolates the interaction of an induced path with two terminal clique symmetries using independent, natural parameters. The complete classification explains both why the known obstruction merges triangle and path vertices and why no further merging survives in arbitrarily large members. It answers a structural question beyond detection of the smallest witness and is not a claim about all block graphs or graph identification.
